lines: I used it and did not drop it. That's two victories, if you ask me.
It did the job when <dark_gray><wavy>fear</wavy></dark_gray> was loud. That is praise enough.
Good gear earns trust the moment trouble tests it.
I swung it at the right thing almost every time.
It has a new scratch. I put that there while remaining alive.
The grip stayed in my hand even when the hand wanted to leave.
I used it until the dangerous part stopped moving toward me.
It worked better than my plan, so I followed the gear instead.
The edge held. My courage bent a little.
I blocked one hit with it and one with a nearby wall.
It felt heavy at first and wonderfully solid after the first noise.
I tested it on real trouble. Real trouble did not enjoy the test.
The strap came loose once, but I noticed before it became exciting.
I used every useful part and avoided the part that looked decorative.
It protected me well enough to bring it back and say so.
I trusted it when my knees had other suggestions.
There is mud on it, but no blood that belongs to me.
It survived the fight in better shape than my hat.
I know how it handles now. Mostly with both hands.
Keep making them like this. I am fond of equipment that returns with me.
I have not used it. I have practiced looking brave with it, which is almost something.
It has stayed clean because trouble has stayed somewhere else.
I carried it all day and never had to discover what this part does.
The edge is untouched. I checked with my eyes, not my thumb.
Nothing attacked us, so the gear spent the trip feeling important.
I kept it ready. Readiness looks a lot like holding something for hours.
It never left its strap, which is the best report I could bring.
I tried the grip twice and the dangerous part zero times.
No dents, no scratches, and no exciting story. Good.
I did not need it. I am strangely proud of that.
The armor stayed new because nothing reached me.
I wore it, sweated in it, and accomplished no fighting at all.
I know where to draw it from now. I did not draw it, but I know.
It is still as sharp as when you gave it to me.
The shield has not blocked anything except a doorway by accident.
I carried it home unused and very slightly heavier from dust.
We saw danger far away. The gear and I agreed to keep it there.
I practiced once on the air. The air recovered quickly.
You can inspect it, but there is no battle hiding in the marks.
I hope it stays unused. It looks happiest that way.
